325314.title: Conjecture on double van der Waerden numbers

literal_record.title: Conjecture on double van der Waerden numbers
literal_record.statement:
Let $w^*(k;a,b)$ denote the least length, when it exists, such that every red-blue coloring of an interval of that length contains the relevant double arithmetic progression with the indicated parameters. The source's tables record computational values and lower bounds for these numbers.

**Double van der Waerden conjecture.** The number $w^*(3,3)$ exists, whereas the number $w^*(2,4)$ does not exist.

325396.title: Exponential Nielsen growth conjecture for infinite finitely generated groups

literal_record.title: Exponential Nielsen growth conjecture for infinite finitely generated groups
literal_record.statement: Let $G$ be an infinite finitely generated group. The **exponential Nielsen growth conjecture** asserts that there are an integer $n$ and a generating $n$-tuple $S\in\Gamma_n(G)$ such that the connected component $\Gamma_n(G,S)$ has exponential growth. This formulation allows product replacement graphs to have multiple connected components and requires growth in only one component. It is weaker than the main conjecture and is known for groups of polynomial or exponential growth, while the general case remains open.
literal_record.source_name: Anton Malyshev and Igor Pak, “Growth in product replacement graphs”, arXiv:1304.5320 (2014).

literal_record.title: Characterization of block graphs by connected fair sets
literal_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A **fair set** of $G$ is a set of vertices whose induced subgraph is under consideration.

**Block-graph characterization conjecture.** The graph $G$ is a block graph if and only if the induced subgraph of every fair set of $G$ is connected.

325401.title: Nevo's Colin de Verdière stress-freeness conjecture

literal_record.title: Nevo's Colin de Verdière stress-freeness conjecture
literal_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $k$ be a positive integer, and let $\mu(G)$ denote the Colin de Verdière parameter of $G$. A graph is **generically $k$-stress free** if it has no nonzero generic $k$-stress. **Nevo's conjecture.** If

$$

$$

then $G$ is generically $k$-stress free. This conjecture is proved in the source for $k=5$ and $k=6$, while the source gives no resolution for the general statement.

325475.title: The equal-slope conjecture for Cookie Monster losing positions

literal_record.title: The equal-slope conjecture for Cookie Monster losing positions
literal_record.statement:
Let $p^0_i,q^0_i$ and $p^1_i,q^1_i$ denote the coordinates of the losing positions of the forms $\{0,p^0_i,q^0_i\}$ and $\{1,p^1_i,q^1_i\}$, respectively. Here, the pairs are compared in their natural order, and the slope of each graph is represented by the ratio of its second coordinate to its first coordinate. **Equal-slope conjecture.** On average, the graphs of $p^0_i$ against $q^0_i$ and $p^1_i$ against $q^1_i$ have the same slope, that is 
$$
\frac{q^0_i}{p^0_i}\approx\frac{q^1_i}{p^1_i}.
$$
 This is an empirical conjecture about the structure of losing positions in the Cookie Monster Problem; the source provides no proof or resolution.
literal_record.source_name: Megan Belzner, “Emptying Sets: The Cookie Monster Problem”, arXiv:1304.7508 (2013).
literal_record.references:

325485.title: Finite-basis conjecture for k-multiplicity-bounded permutations

literal_record.title: Finite-basis conjecture for k-multiplicity-bounded permutations
literal_record.statement:
For an integer $k\geq1$, a permutation $w$ is **$k$-multiplicity bounded** when every coefficient $a_{w\lambda}$ in the Schur expansion

$$
F_w=\sum_{\lambda}a_{w\lambda}s_{\lambda}
$$

satisfies $a_{w\lambda}\leq k$. **Finite-basis conjecture for $k$-multiplicity-bounded permutations.** For each fixed $k$, the $k$-multiplicity-bounded permutations are characterized by avoiding a finite set of permutation patterns. Pattern containment already preserves this property; the conjecture asserts that the minimal excluded patterns have bounded size.
literal_record.source_name: Sara Billey and Brendan Pawlowski, “Permutation patterns, Stanley symmetric functions and generalized Specht modules”, arXiv:1304.7870 (2013).

325526.title: Brualdi's conjecture in rainbow-matching form

literal_record.title: Brualdi's conjecture in rainbow-matching form
literal_record.statement:
Let $K_{n,n}$ be the complete bipartite graph, and suppose its edges are partitioned into $n$ matchings, each of size $n$. A **rainbow matching** is a matching containing at most one edge from each part of the partition.

**Brualdi's conjecture.** Such a partition has a rainbow matching of size $n-1$.

This is the rainbow-matching formulation of Brualdi's conjecture that every Latin square of even order $n$ has a partial transversal of size $n-1$. The supplied source presents it as a known conjecture and does not report a resolution.

325566.title: Huang–Wong–Zhu on-line Ohba conjecture

literal_record.title: Huang–Wong–Zhu on-line Ohba conjecture
literal_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $|V(G)|$ and $\chi(G)$ denote its number of vertices and chromatic number, respectively. A graph is **on-line chromatic-choosable** if $\chi_p(G)=\chi(G)$. **Huang–Wong–Zhu's conjecture.** Every graph $G$ with

$$
|V(G)|\leq 2\chi(G)

is on-line chromatic-choosable. The source introduces this as an on-line version of Ohba's conjecture; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.

325648.title: Generalized Ryser–Brualdi–Stein matching conjecture

literal_record.title: Generalized Ryser–Brualdi–Stein matching conjecture
literal_record.statement:
Let $H$ be a simple $d$-regular $3$-partite $3$-uniform hypergraph whose three sides each have size $n$, so that $H$ is an $n\times n\times n$ $3$-partite hypergraph. A **matching** is a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges. **Generalized Ryser–Brualdi–Stein conjecture.** The hypergraph $H$ contains a matching of size at least

$$
\left\lceil\frac{d-1}{d}n\right\rceil.
$$

This is proposed as a further generalization of the Latin-square conjectures, under the explicit assumption that repeated edges are absent; the source gives no resolution.
literal_record.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Pierre Charbit and David Howard, “On a Generalization of the Ryser-Brualdi-Stein Conjecture”, arXiv:1305.6164 (2013).
literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.6164

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2013). “For even $n$ this is false, and Brualdi and Stein raised independently the following natural conjecture: In a Latin square of order $n$ there exists a partial transversal of size $n-1$.”

325979.title: Lin et al.'s distance spectral characterization conjecture for complete multipartite graphs

literal_record.title: Lin et al.'s distance spectral characterization conjecture for complete multipartite graphs
literal_record.statement:
Let $G=K_{n_1,n_2,...,n_k}$ be a complete $k$-partite graph. For a graph $H$, let $Sp(D(H))$ denote the multiset of eigenvalues of its distance matrix, and say that $G$ is **determined by its D-spectrum** when $Sp(D(G))=Sp(D(H))$ implies $G\cong H$. **Lin et al.'s conjecture.** The graph $G$ is determined by its D-spectrum.

This conjecture concerns whether complete multipartite graphs are uniquely determined by the spectra of their distance matrices, in contrast with their failure to be determined by adjacency spectra. The paper's abstract states that the conjecture is confirmed by the paper's proof.
literal_record.source_name: Ya-Lei Jin and Xiao-Dong Zhang, “Complete multipartite graphs are determined by their distance spectra”, arXiv:1307.5931 (2013).

326136.title: Formation width conjecture for $abc(acb)^t abc$

literal_record.title: Formation width conjecture for $abc(acb)^t abc$
literal_record.statement:
Let $t$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $\mathit{fw}(u)$ denote the formation width of a sequence $u$. **Formation width conjecture.**

$$
\mathit{fw}(abc(acb)^{t}abc)=2t+3.
$$

The paper states that this would imply nearly tight bounds on the extremal function $\mathit{Ex}(abc(acb)^{t}abc,n)$. The conjecture extends the proved result $\mathit{fw}(abc(acb)^t)=2t+1$ for $t\geq 0$; its resolution is not given here.
literal_record.source_name: J. T. Geneson, Rohil Prasad and Jonathan Tidor, “Bounding sequence extremal functions with formations”, arXiv:1308.3810 (2014).

326140.title: The unique-subsequence-sum conjecture for zero-sum free sequences

literal_record.title: The unique-subsequence-sum conjecture for zero-sum free sequences
literal_record.statement: Let $p$ be prime, let $k$ be a positive integer, and let $G=C_p^k$. A sequence over $G$ is **zero-sum free** if none of its nonempty subsequences has sum zero. **The short-subsequence conjecture.** If $T$ is a zero-sum free indexed sequence over $G=C_p^k$, then there exists a subsequence $T_0$ of $T$ with length less than $p$ such that no other subsequence of $T$ has the same sum as $T_0$. This conjecture is intended to control long irreducible subsequences and would imply the elementary abelian $p$-group case of the $\mathsf{N}_{1}$ conjecture; the context notes that the assertion is trivial when $|T|<p$, but gives no general proof.
literal_record.source_name: Xiaoyu He, “Cross Number Invariants of Finite Abelian Groups”, arXiv:1308.3896 (2013).
literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.3896

326141.title: The cyclic-subgroup strengthening for zero-sum free sequences

literal_record.title: The cyclic-subgroup strengthening for zero-sum free sequences
literal_record.statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $k$ be a positive integer, and let $G=C_p^k$. For a cyclic subgroup $H$ of $G$, let $T_H$ denote the subsequence of $T$ consisting of terms in $H$, and let $\Sigma(U)$ denote the set of subsequence sums of a sequence $U$. **The cyclic-subgroup strengthening.** If $T$ is a zero-sum free indexed sequence over $G=C_p^k$, then there exists a cyclic subgroup $H$ of $G$ such that $T_H\neq 1$ and

$$
H\cap\Sigma\left(T(T_H)^{-1}\right)=\emptyset.
$$

This is presented as a strengthening of the preceding short-subsequence conjecture and is likewise proposed to help resolve the elementary abelian $p$-group case; no resolution is supplied.
literal_record.source_name: Xiaoyu He, “Cross Number Invariants of Finite Abelian Groups”, arXiv:1308.3896 (2013).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.3896

326178.title: The regular-simplex conjecture for unions of spherical caps

literal_record.title: The regular-simplex conjecture for unions of spherical caps
literal_record.statement:
Let $S$ be a sphere in the $n$-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$, and let $n+1$ spherical caps on $S$ have the same prescribed radius. Among all configurations of their centers, consider one maximizing the volume of their union.

**Regular-simplex conjecture.** The maximizing configuration is always the one in which the $n+1$ centers are the vertices of a regular simplex in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

The source describes this as an innocent-looking and plausible conjecture, open in dimension $n\geq4$. It is a geometric extremal problem related to spherical arrangements and cap unions.
literal_record.source_name: Viktor Harangi and Bálint Virág, “Independence ratio and random eigenvectors in transitive graphs”, arXiv:1308.5173 (2015).
literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.5173

326295.title: The lexicographic shellability conjecture for the electrical poset

literal_record.title: The lexicographic shellability conjecture for the electrical poset
literal_record.statement: Let $EP_n$ be the graded poset of electrical networks on $n$ boundary vertices, with rank given by the number of edges in a critical representative. **Lexicographic shellability conjecture.** $EP_n$ is lexicographically shellable, and hence Cohen–Macaulay, spherical, and Eulerian. This would give strong topological information about the order complex of $EP_n$. The text reports verification of the Eulerian property for $n\leq 7$, agreement of homology with a sphere for $n\leq 4$, and no known $L$-labeling for $n\geq 4$; the general conjecture remains open.
literal_record.source_name: Joshua Alman, Carl Lian and Brandon Tran, “Circular Planar Electrical Networks I: The Electrical Poset EP_n”, arXiv:1309.2697 (2013).
literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.2697
